subject: Customer Security Q: Hosted API data locality, TTLs, and erasure steps

Subject: Hosted API questionnaire - data locality + TTLs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for agreeing to take our security questionnaire. We've attached a short set of questions focused on hosted API data locality, retention, and deletion workflows. At a high level:

- Do you offer region-bound hosting for customer data? If so, which regions are available and how is geography enforced?
- What are typical retention TTLs for request logs vs. model input/output vs. embeddings?
- What is your standard timeframe for complete customer data erasure on request (including backups)?
- Where can we find evidence of audited deletion (audit logs / attestations)?

We're hoping to include this in our privacy review for a POC. Please see the attached questionnaire and send any supporting docs you can share.

Hi Liz — thanks for sending this over. I've answered the questions inline below and attached a short SLA excerpt that covers erasure commitments and backups. I'm cc'ing Kimberly (product security) and Priyom (support/ops) to help with any follow-ups and to provide logs/evidence if you need it.

1) Region-bound hosting:
- We offer hosted API deployments with customer data pinned to region clusters: US (us-west-2, us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1), and APAC (ap-southeast-1) for customers on our regional hosting plan.
- Geography is enforced at the routing and storage layer: requests are routed to the regional serving pool, and persistent logs/embeddings are written only to region-specific object stores and databases. Networking rules (VPC peering and subnet restrictions) and IAM policies prevent cross-region data replication for region-scoped tenants.

2) Retention TTLs (defaults and examples):
- Request logs (ingestion metadata and routing traces): default 90 days; optional 30/365 day tiers for enterprise customers.
- Model input/output payloads (hosted API request/response content): ephemeral by default (24 hours) and purged automatically; persistent storage is only used if customer enables "retain transcripts". If retained, default TTL is 365 days unless configured otherwise.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: retained only when customer creates an embeddings index or enables retention; default TTL 730 days for retained indexes.

3) Erasure timeframe (hosted API):
- For active data (non-backup): logical deletion completes within 48 hours and is reflected in tenant-level views immediately.
- For backups/snapshots: backups are included in a periodic snapshot rotation. We guarantee that deleted tenant data will be removed from active backups within the next backup cycle and fully expunged within 30 days. Enterprise customers can contract for accelerated removal windows (7–14 days).

4) Evidence & audit logs:
- We maintain immutable audit logs for deletion actions (who requested, when, and job IDs) that can be exported to customer accounts or shared under NDA.
- SOC 2 report and deletion attestation excerpts can be shared with signed NDA.

Attachments: [redwood-erasure-sla-sample.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]

If helpful, we can provide an export of the deletion job records (sample format) and a short recording outlining the technical flow. Happy to set up a 30-minute call.

Thanks,

Liz — quick follow-up with the specific confirmations you requested: 

- Backups & encryption/replication: snapshots are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys for enterprise accounts (BYOK) and AES-256 for standard plans. By default we retain cross-region replication only for customers who opt into our multi-region DR offering; replication is documented and controlled by the tenant settings and requires an explicit opt-in. For Acme's POC, we will keep backups within the US region unless you request DR replication in contract.

- Embeddings & backup window: yes — any persisted embeddings index follows the same backup rotation policy. If you request deletion of the index, logical deletion is immediate and we schedule expunge from backups within the 30-day window; we can contract for a 7–14 day accelerated expunge for enterprise customers.

- Audit exports: deletion job exports are JSONL (each line is an event) and include job_id, object_type, object_id, requested_by, initiated_at, completed_at (when completed). We can provide an export within 48 hours of job completion; for large jobs we publish a download link to your secure bucket.

Next steps: Kimberly and Priyom, can you prepare a sample deletion-job export (sanitized) and the SOC 2 extract under NDA this week? Liz — if that works for you, let's schedule a 30-minute sync (I can loop in Product Ops) to walk through the export format and SLA clauses.

Thanks all,
Jonas
